headline: Cheyenne and Arapaho tribal citizens voted to ban data center construction on their land in Oklahoma for three years.
score_reason: Pool 5 kept: a clear vote with exact numbers and a notable split with tribal leadership; local scale. Event was 3 Oct, one day old, so not lowered.
importance_line: Tribal members, who would have borne water and land impacts, decided against the view of their governor, who saw income for elders and housing, but no project had been signed and no site had been named.
summary: News 9 reports that Cheyenne and Arapaho tribal citizens voted 261 to 83, with 7 abstentions, on Saturday 3 Oct 2026 to impose a three-year moratorium (a pause) on data center construction on tribal land. Speakers raised worries about water use and transparency, while Governor Reggie Wassanna argued that modern closed-loop cooling uses little water and that a data center could bring the tribe large income.
notes: Vote day inferred from 'Saturday' in an article published 4 Oct 2026 US time. Governor's spelling follows the article.
